learning: Slalom steering_oscillation sat at about 0.14 across leads y=0.05, 0.06 and 0.07 m, so the lead is not the jitter driver. If oscillation stays above 0.10 with zero line loss, speed or controller tuning is the next lever, not geometry.
notes: Integrator package for the wheel_radius test. Only wheel_radius differs from iteration 3, so the race isolates ground speed at the best sensor lead (y=0.07 m).
rationale: Iteration 3 (y=0.07 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m) is the best raced design at 51.31. Its s-bend progress reached 0.155, but it had one line-loss event per run on s-bend and slalom, and slalom steering_oscillation was 0.138. Slalom oscillation has stayed at about 0.14 at every tested lead (y=0.05, 0.06, 0.07 m), so the lead is not what drives it. The oval has been fixed at progress 0.115 and max_error 0.061 m since iteration 1. The Builder's intent is one change from iteration 3: wheel_radius 0.03 to 0.04 m, which raises ground speed by about 33%. I keep the controller identical to iteration 3 (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.10, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]) so the race result is attributable to wheel_radius alone. The sensor spread (+/-0.05 m) and 16 mm footprints stay, since they gave zero line loss in iteration 1. The main risk is that the higher speed brings back line loss on the bends, which would show that the speed limit is the constraint.
